author: W. Oelen
caption: Copper sulfate as large blue crystals (top) and as a fine powder (bottom) — the same salt in both forms.

author: Andrew Silver
caption: Halite is natural sodium chloride (rock salt); these crystals come from the Fayoum region of Egypt.

author: Adam Rędzikowski
caption: Needle-shaped crystals of potassium nitrate. Crystals like these form when a hot, saturated solution cools, because the salt is much less soluble in cold water.

author: Mark Dumont
caption: A cheetah is the fastest land animal: in a short sprint it can reach about 30 m/s, which is over 100 km/h.

author: Gmihail at Serbian Wikipedia
caption: A seesaw in a garden in Hurghada: the pivot is in the middle, so a lighter person must sit further from the pivot to balance a heavier one.

author: A Burqa
caption: A camel's feet are wide and padded, so its weight is spread over a large area and the pressure on soft sand is small.

author: Billertl
caption: Snowshoes have a very large area, which lowers the pressure on the snow so the walker does not sink in.

author: Alessandro e Damiano
caption: Purple potassium permanganate spreading through water: with time its particles intermingle with the water particles until the colour is even.

author: Oregon's Mt. Hood Territory
caption: Still water is very smooth, so it gives regular reflection and a clear, upside-down image of the mountain (Mount Hood, Oregon, USA).

author: ajizai
caption: A real light ray bends as it enters and leaves a glass block; the ray that comes out is parallel to the ray that went in.

author: Meganbeckett27
caption: Refraction makes the pencil look bent (and broken) where it enters the water, although it is really straight.

author: Kelvinsong
caption: A glass prism disperses white light into a spectrum, from red (bent least) to violet (bent most).

author: Kreuzschnabel
caption: A rainbow: sunlight is dispersed by raindrops, so red is on the outside of the arc and violet on the inside.

author: MikeRun, Vera Wurmsdobler
caption: Iron filings line up along the field lines of a bar magnet and crowd together at the poles, where the field is strongest.

author: MikeRun, Vera Wurmsdobler
caption: With a south pole facing a north pole, the filings make lines that run across the gap from one magnet to the other — the magnets attract.

author: Evan-Amos
caption: The needle of a compass is a tiny magnet that lines up with the Earth's magnetic field; its red (north-seeking) end is marked.

author: Hatem Moushir
caption: Wind turbines at Zafarana on the Gulf of Suez coast, one of the windiest places in Egypt.

author: Silar
caption: The Aswan High Dam: water from Lake Nasser flows through turbines to generate hydroelectric power, which leaves through the switchyard and power lines in front.

author: Steve Hillebrand, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
caption: A U-shaped valley: a glacier carved this wide, flat-bottomed shape, so U-shaped valleys in places with no ice today show that glaciers were once there.

author: Kurinurm
caption: An erratic boulder: ice sheets carried rocks like this far from where they formed and dropped them when the ice melted.

author: Helle Astrid Kjær
caption: A freshly cut section of an ice core from Greenland: the ice holds tiny bubbles of old air that scientists can analyse.

author: T. J. Casadevall, U.S. Geological Survey
caption: Mount Pinatubo erupting in June 1991: ash and gases thrown high into the atmosphere blocked some sunlight and cooled the Earth slightly for about two years.

author: Bruno Gilli/ESO
caption: The Milky Way seen from a dark desert in Chile: the bright band is the disc of our galaxy, with dark dust clouds; the two small smudges on the left are the Magellanic Clouds.

author: Adam Evans
caption: The Andromeda Galaxy, a spiral galaxy about 2.5 million light-years away; the light from it left about 2.5 million years ago.

author: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA/MPS/DLR/IDA
caption: Vesta, about 525 km across, photographed by NASA's Dawn spacecraft: it is cratered and not perfectly round.

author: NASA/Goddard/University of Arizona
caption: The small asteroid Bennu, photographed by NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft, which brought a sample of its rock back to the Earth in 2023.
